levels.title: Primitives
levels.definition: The smallest working pieces and the base styles. A primitive contains no other ORCA element.
levels.examples: button, input, icon, text style, status mark, token.

levels.title: Components
levels.definition: A group of primitives with one job.
levels.examples: form field, search bar, date picker, pagination, stat card, toast.

levels.title: Patterns
levels.definition: A group of components that forms a recognisable section of a page.
levels.examples: page head with page actions, filter drawer, sidebar, data table, month calendar.

levels.title: Templates
levels.definition: A group of patterns arranged into a page layout, with placeholder content.
levels.examples: app shell, list page, detail page, form page, calendar page.

levels.title: Pages
levels.definition: A template filled with real content, including the variations that test it.
levels.examples: a list page shown empty, overdue, right-to-left and dark.

brand_tokens.usage: Product name. Used by the Logo primitive as the wordmark and as the logo's alt text.
Static path of the logo image (SVG preferred), e.g. 'brand/logo.svg'. Empty: the Logo shows the name as a wordmark.
Static path of a 32px PNG or an SVG favicon. Empty: no favicon tags are written.

The brand colour. Decorative brand marks and the 3px brand bars use it as given. ORCA derives --orca-brand-strong (fills that carry text, darkened until --orca-brand-on reads at 4.5:1), --orca-brand-strong-hover and --orca-brand-strong-active from it, and the top bar ground --orca-brand-bar (the colour mixed with 30% black, as in wise_people_analyzer) with --orca-brand-bar-on, -hover and -active.
Text and icons on brand fills. Empty: ORCA picks black or white, whichever reads better.

The interactive colour of the light and paper themes: links, checked ticks and radios, switches that are on, progress fills, selected days. ORCA darkens it if it falls below 4.5:1 on the page grounds.
The interactive colour in the dark theme. Empty: derived from 'accent', lightened until it reads at 4.5:1 on #262626.

brand_tokens.default: "Ubuntu Sans", -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif
brand_tokens.usage: Font stack for all interface text. ORCA self-hosts Ubuntu Sans (variable, 100–800). A replacement face must have regular (400) and semibold (550 or 600) weights and you must load it yourself.
Font stack for code, keyboard keys and tabular identifiers. ORCA self-hosts JetBrains Mono (variable, 100–800, Latin and Latin Extended); "Ubuntu Sans Mono" is also bundled if you prefer it.

categories.title: Base styles
categories.intro: Tokens every other element is built from: colour, type, space, shape, elevation, layers, size and motion. Use these names, never raw values. Only brand tokens may be changed by a project.

categories.title: Text
categories.intro: Text styles with a fixed role. Choose by what the text is (a page title, a stat value), not by how big you want it.

categories.title: Form text
categories.intro: The words around a field: its label, requirement marker, help and errors. They decide whether a form is completed.

categories.title: Actions
categories.intro: Things people press. One primary action per screen; everything else is quieter.

categories.title: Inputs
categories.intro: Native form controls styled by ORCA. Native first: they work with keyboards, screen readers, autofill and phones for free.

categories.title: Icons
categories.intro: One icon set, 16px, single ink in currentColor. Icons support words; they never replace them.

categories.title: Status marks and labels
categories.intro: Small marks that state a condition or categorise an item. Status always pairs colour with a word and, where it matters, a shape.

categories.title: Identity
categories.intro: Who and what: the product's logo and favicon, and people's avatars.

categories.title: Imagery
categories.intro: Images, frames and graphics. Reserve their space, describe them, and keep text readable over them.

categories.title: Structure marks
categories.intro: Marks that organise and connect: rules, separators, focus, markers and backdrops. Plus the accessibility helpers every page needs.

categories.title: Progress
categories.intro: Feedback while something takes time. Respond within 400 ms; show progress for longer; describe the step past 10 seconds.

categories.title: Chart and graphic marks
categories.intro: The small marks charts, legends, zones and heat maps are made of. Every colour mark has a text label nearby.

categories.title: Planning inputs
categories.intro: Date, time and schedule inputs. Native pickers first: they are what people already know, on every device.

categories.title: Planning text
categories.intro: How dates, times and durations are written. Always machine-readable (`<time datetime>`) and formatted for the reader's locale and timezone.

categories.title: Planning marks
categories.intro: Marks drawn on calendars, schedules and timelines. Each state pairs colour with a shape, a pattern or a word.

categories.title: Planning icons
categories.intro: Icons for time and scheduling ideas, drawn by ORCA on the same 16px grid as the rest of the set.

categories.title: Forms
categories.intro: Fields and the small groups around them. A form field is the unit people complete: label, hint, error and control in a fixed order.

categories.title: Navigation
categories.intro: How people move between places and pages. The current location is always marked with aria-current and a shape, not only colour.

categories.title: Feedback
categories.intro: How the system tells people what happened and what to do next: alerts, callouts, toasts, dialogs, empty states and progress.

categories.title: Actions
categories.intro: Groups of actions: button groups, menus and the action sets that sit on records and rows.

categories.title: Data display
categories.intro: Ways to present records and numbers: stat cards, lists, key/value lists, cards, tables, timelines and small charts.

categories.title: Content blocks
categories.intro: Reusable blocks for products, people, posts, heroes and media.

categories.title: Identity and controls
categories.intro: Who is signed in, what a panel is, and the small controls that personalise the interface.

categories.title: Date and time pickers
categories.intro: Native date and time inputs, composed with shortcuts, ranges, time zones and a month grid. Native first: every device already knows how to pick a date.

categories.title: Planning selectors
categories.intro: Controls that choose days, repeats, reminders, periods, granularity and calendar views.

categories.title: Calendar parts
categories.intro: The pieces month, week, day and agenda views are built from. Each states the date in words for screen readers.

categories.title: Schedule parts
categories.intro: Rows and messages for opening hours, availability, exceptions, time off and bookings.

categories.title: Plan items
categories.intro: Tasks, milestones, deadlines and reminders, and the chips that describe them: assignee, due date, status, priority, progress.

categories.title: Documentation site
categories.intro: Components for documenting a design system or an API: live examples, code blocks and the navigation tree.

categories.title: Page frame
categories.intro: The parts every page sits in: headers, top bar, sidebar, footer, page head, messages, drawers and filter panels.

categories.title: Grids and collections
categories.intro: Repeating one component in a responsive grid or sequence: products, videos, KPIs, a heat map, an event timeline.

categories.title: Data and filtering
categories.intro: Tables, panels and the controls that narrow them: filter bars, list headers, summary tiles and record cards.

categories.title: Forms
categories.intro: Whole form sections and specialised editors: sections, stacks, sign-in, schedules, zones, properties and rich text.

categories.title: Media
categories.intro: Video players, live streams, photo posts and image galleries.

categories.title: Record management
categories.intro: Showing and changing one record and its children: detail panels, child tabs, activity, protected deletes and confirmations.

categories.title: Charts
categories.intro: Charts drawn by Chart.js in a chart frame, in token colours, each with a text summary and its data as a table. One template tag; no chart code to write.

categories.title: Marketing and documentation site
categories.intro: Sections for a product's public pages and its documentation: hero, features, live tokens, code samples and docs navigation.

categories.title: Process and status
categories.intro: Following a long-running job: what is done, what is happening, what failed and what to do.

categories.title: Editorial
categories.intro: Blocks for stories and highlighted facts on news, blog and report pages.

categories.title: Email
categories.intro: The frame every transactional email is written in: brand bar, title, text, one action, footer.

categories.title: Calendar views
categories.intro: Whole calendars rendered on the server from a list of events: month, week, day, multi-day, agenda and year, plus the toolbar, sidebar and legend around them.

categories.title: Scheduler
categories.intro: Editing when things and people are available, and booking time against that availability.

categories.title: Event editing
categories.intro: Creating, viewing and answering events: full editor, popover, panel, quick add, reminders, attendees and RSVP.

categories.title: Planning boards and timelines
categories.intro: Seeing and steering work over time: task lists, boards, Gantt charts, roadmaps, milestones, capacity, deadlines and plan summaries.

categories.title: Layouts
categories.intro: Whole-page Django templates you extend. They place patterns in a fixed structure and leave named blocks for your content. Every page of an ORCA project starts from one of these.

categories.title: Page-type skeletons
categories.intro: The app shell set up for one kind of screen: dashboard, calendar, scheduler, board, timeline, booking, event editor and simple data page. Pass data in the context; override a block only to change a region.

categories.title: Structural layouts
categories.intro: Layout classes that arrange sections inside a page: stacks, grids and splits. They hold patterns and never style them.

categories.title: Template slots
categories.intro: The named blocks of ORCA's layouts. A page fills slots instead of rewriting layouts, so every page keeps the same structure. Each slot below says which layouts have it and what belongs in it.

elements.name: Colour palette
elements.summary: Raw colours: a 13-step gray scale and eleven hues with nine numbered steps each.
elements.why: A small, named palette keeps colour consistent and lets semantic tokens point at known values (Practical UI C18: name raw colours separately from their uses). Generating the hues in OKLCH gives every step the same perceived lightness across hues, so a chart's series read as equally important.
when: Charts, zones, calendars and illustrations that need several distinguishable categories.
Defining a new semantic token inside ORCA itself.
how: Gray: `--orca-gray-0` (white) to `--orca-gray-1000` (black), Tangerine's values.
Hues: `--orca-{red|orange|amber|yellow|green|teal|cyan|blue|indigo|purple|pink}-{100..900}`; 100 is lightest.
For data series prefer `--orca-chart-1`…`--orca-chart-8`, which already pick contrasting steps per theme.
Text on a hue step: steps 100–400 take `--orca-text` in light themes; 600–900 take white.
avoid: Text, controls, grounds and status: use semantic tokens (`semantic-colors`) instead.
Telling two series apart by hue alone: change lightness or add a shape, label or pattern.

examples.title: Gray and one hue

law_names: Practical UI C18: Name raw colours separately from their uses
Practical UI C03: Communicate meaning beyond colour
Aesthetic–usability effect: consistent, careful visuals earn trust

elements.name: Semantic colour tokens
elements.summary: Colours named by their job: text, grounds, lines, interaction, status, actions, planning, data.
elements.why: Components written against roles (`--orca-text-muted`, `--orca-border-strong`) work in every theme without change, and every role carries a tested contrast promise (Practical UI C09, C01).
when: Every colour in every element and page.
how: Text: `text` (body, labels, headings), `text-muted` (help, meta), `text-inactive` (unselected nav).
Grounds: `bg` page, `bg-alt` set-apart region, `bg-input` fields, `bg-hover`, `bg-active` (pressed, selected), `bg-elevated` floating.
Lines: `border` decorative, `border-strong` controls, `border-weak` row separators.
Status families `info`, `positive`, `caution`, `negative`, `neutral`: the bare name for marks and text, `-bg` for tints, `-fill` for solid badges.
Actions: `primary*` (main action, green), `danger*` (confirmed destruction), `brand-strong*` (brand fill).
Pair every status colour with an icon and a word.
avoid: Choosing a token for how it looks rather than what it is for (a muted heading is still `--orca-text`).
Using `--orca-border` (decorative, 1.6:1) on a control: controls need `--orca-border-strong` (3:1).
a11y: `text` and `text-muted` hold 4.5:1 on `bg`, `bg-alt` and `bg-input` in every theme.
Known exception kept from Vanilla: `caution` as text is 3.0:1 in light; never set caution text alone.

examples.html:

Secondary text uses --orca-text-muted.

law_names: Practical UI C09: Give each palette token a role
Practical UI C18: Name raw colours separately from their uses
Practical UI C01: Check contrast for meaningful content
Practical UI C04: Reserve status colours for their meanings

elements.name: Brand colour and surfaces
elements.summary: The one brand colour, the fills derived from it, and the page surfaces it sits on.
elements.why: One brand colour plus neutrals is usually enough (Practical UI C07). Deriving the text-carrying fill automatically keeps any brand colour readable, moving the contrast work from the developer to the system (Tesler's law).
when: The one brand moment on a page: the top bar, the brand button, the logo mark, a highlight rule.
Re-branding a deployment: set `ORCA['BRAND']['color']` and nothing else.
how: `--orca-brand`: the colour as given, for decorative marks and 3px bars (needs only 3:1).
`--orca-brand-strong`: fills that carry text; darkened by ORCA until `--orca-brand-on` reads at 4.5:1.
`--orca-brand-strong-hover` / `-active`: hover and pressed fills, derived.
Surfaces: page `--orca-bg`, set-apart regions `--orca-bg-alt`, floating `--orca-bg-elevated`.
Set it in settings; ORCA reports any adjustment it made as a system-check warning (`orca.W001`).
avoid: More than one brand-filled element per screen (Von Restorff: emphasis loses power when repeated).
Status meaning: brand is never success, warning or error.
Links and checked controls: those use the accent colour.
a11y: Never rely on brand colour alone to show state; selection uses the accent and a shape.

examples.title: Brand moments
examples.html: {% orca_logo href="" %}

law_names: Practical UI C07: Prefer one purposeful action colour
Practical UI C08: Choose and adapt the brand colour deliberately
Von Restorff effect: the one thing that differs is noticed; use emphasis sparingly
Tesler's law: move unavoidable complexity from the user to the system

elements.name: Accent colour
elements.summary: The single interactive colour: links, checked ticks, radios, switches, progress, selected days.
elements.why: One consistent action colour teaches people what they can act on (Practical UI C07); using it for every 'on' state makes selection recognisable at a glance.
when: Text links, the checked state of ticks, radios and switches, progress fills, selected calendar days, accent outlines and accent badges.
how: Use `var(--orca-accent)`; hover is `var(--orca-accent-hover)`.
Brand token: `ORCA['BRAND']['accent']` (light and paper) and optional `accent_dark`; ORCA darkens or lightens it to 4.5:1.
Text on an accent fill is `var(--orca-bg)`.
avoid: Static headings or decorative icons: action colour on non-interactive things misleads (C07).
Large fills behind long text.
a11y: Holds 4.5:1 on `bg` and `bg-alt` in every theme, so it can be used for link text.

examples.title: Accent in use
examples.html: Read the retention policy.

law_names: Practical UI C07: Prefer one purposeful action colour
Jakob's law: work the way products people already know work

elements.name: Themes
elements.summary: Light, dark and paper share every token name. ORCA has one appearance: Tangerine.
elements.why: Writing components once against shared names means a theme can never break a component (Postel's law: reliable output in every context). Users with light sensitivity or bright surroundings choose what suits them.
when: Always: every page supports all three themes for free.
Set `ORCA['THEME']` to `light`, `dark` or `paper` to force one; `auto` (default) follows the OS and the user's stored choice.
how: Put `{% orca_html_attrs %}` on `<html>` and `{% orca_head %}` in `<head>`.
A theme toggle is a button with `data-orca-theme-toggle`; it cycles light → dark → paper and remembers the choice.
Appearance: Tangerine only (square corners, 1.5px borders, filled fields with a bottom border, inside focus ring).
avoid: Theme-specific CSS in your own code: if something needs it, the token is missing; report it.
Pure black grounds: dark uses #262626 and #202020.
a11y: Contrast promises hold in every theme; dark lifts floating surfaces one step so elevation shows without shadows.

examples.title: Theme toggle
examples.html: <button class="orca-icon-button orca-icon-button--outlined" type="button" data-orca-theme-toggle aria-label="Change theme">{% icon "sun" %}</button>

law_names: Postel's law: accept varied input, output reliable and accessible UI
Practical UI C11: Build dark palettes independently
Practical UI C12: Use elevation consistently

elements.name: Fonts and type styles
elements.summary: Ubuntu Sans (variable) for everything, JetBrains Mono for code, on a fixed type scale.
elements.why: One legible sans serif with two working weights keeps the interface calm and readable (Practical UI T01, T04); a fixed scale makes hierarchy predictable (T05).
when: Every piece of text. Pick the style by role: heading, title, body, detail, label, code.
how: Heading: `--orca-type-h1`…`h6`, `--orca-type-page-title`, `--orca-type-display`.
Title: `--orca-type-title` (panel and card titles, 18/24 550).
Body: `--orca-type-body` (16/24) and `--orca-type-body-strong` (550). Bold is 550, not 700.
Detail: `--orca-type-detail` (14/20) for help, meta and timestamps; `--orca-type-label` (12/16 550) for table headers, badges, kickers and stat card labels.
Figure: `--orca-type-figure` (28/36 550) for the number of a stat card.
Code: `--orca-type-code` with `--orca-font-mono` (JetBrains Mono, self-hosted; it tells 0/O and 1/l/I apart). Code blocks are coloured with the `--orca-code-*` tokens.
Numbers in tables and stats get `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` (`.orca-num`).
Use as `font: var(--orca-type-body)`. Brand tokens `font_sans` / `font_mono` swap the families.
avoid: New sizes or weights in page CSS.
Weights other than 400 and 550 for interface text (thin 180/275 only for the large h2/h4 styles).
All caps for anything longer than a short label (W07).
a11y: Sizes are in rem so they follow the user's font-size setting; the root grows to 18px above 1681px.
Running text is capped at `--orca-measure` (70ch).

law_names: Practical UI T01: One legible sans serif family
Practical UI T04: Limit the working set of weights
Practical UI T05: Build sizes from a type scale
Practical UI T07: Comfortable line spacing
Practical UI T09: Limit reading measure
Aesthetic–usability effect: consistent, careful visuals earn trust

elements.name: Spacing scale
elements.summary: Eleven spacing steps on the 8px unit, named by their pixel value.
elements.why: A small set of spacing options removes guesswork and makes grouping visible: related things sit closer than unrelated things (Miller's law, Practical UI L08, L09).
when: Every margin, padding and gap.
how: `--orca-space-4` menu rows · `-8` icon to label, related controls, label to field · `-12` field to help text · `-16` button and input side padding, card padding, between fields · `-24` between sections · `-32` between page regions · `-48` alert text inset.
Work from the inside out: the innermost gap is smallest.
Utilities: `.orca-stack` (column, 8px), `.orca-row` (wrapping row, 8px; `.orca-row--16`).
avoid: Values off the scale (6px, 10px, 18px).
The same small gap at every nesting level: it flattens grouping.

law_names: Miller's law: chunk information so working memory is not overloaded
Practical UI L08: Define a limited spacing scale
Practical UI L09: Set spacing by relationship
Practical UI L01: Group related information

elements.name: Borders
elements.summary: Three line weights: 1px hairline, 1.5px outline, 3px emphasis bar.
elements.why: Consistent line weights make structure readable without decoration (Practical UI S02); the 3px bar is reserved for emphasis so it keeps its meaning.
when: Hairline: rules, table header line, row separators.
1.5px: outlines of buttons, cards, alerts, tick boxes; the field bottom border.
3px: the selected tab, an alert's side bar, the focus ring, a highlight rule.
how: Width tokens: `--orca-hairline`, `--orca-border-width`, `--orca-bar`.
Colour tokens: `--orca-border` (decorative), `--orca-border-strong` (controls, 3:1), `--orca-border-weak` (rows).
avoid: Borders that box every group (Practical UI L01): use space first.

examples.title: Three weights

law_names: Practical UI R18: Keep control boundaries visible
Practical UI S02: Remove styles that compete without communicating

elements.name: Corner radii
elements.summary: Tangerine is square; only round marks and bar ends are rounded.
elements.why: One consistent shape language is part of the system's recognisable look (Aesthetic–usability effect); rounding reserved for round marks (radios, dots, avatars) keeps those marks distinct from boxes (checkboxes).
when: `--orca-radius-none` for every box: buttons, fields, cards, menus, dialogs, badges, tags.
`--orca-radius-round` for radios, status dots, avatars, step markers, the switch handle.
`--orca-radius-pill` for the switch track and count badges; `--orca-radius-bar` for progress tracks.
how: Use the tokens even for 0 so a future rounding change is a token change, not a hunt.
avoid: Rounding a checkbox: the square box versus round radio is how people tell one-of-many from many (Practical UI R07).

examples.title: Shapes
examples.html: AL 3

law_names: Aesthetic–usability effect: consistent, careful visuals earn trust
Practical UI R07: Keep recognisable control features

elements.name: Shadows and elevation
elements.summary: Three shadows (card, elevated, dragged) and elevation utilities. Only floating things cast a shadow.
elements.why: Depth signals what sits above the page and what can be moved (Practical UI C12, L05). Reserving shadows for floating things keeps them meaningful.
when: `shadow-card`: the hover lift of an interactive card.
`shadow-elevated`: menus, dropdown lists, popovers, toasts, drawers.
`shadow-dragged`: a dragged item, a dialog, a sidebar opened over content.
how: Utilities: `.orca-elevation-0` … `.orca-elevation-3` (2 and 3 also set `--orca-bg-elevated`).
In dark themes elevation also comes from the lighter `--orca-bg-elevated` surface.
avoid: Shadows on cards at rest, panels or page sections: use a border or `bg-alt`.

law_names: Practical UI C12: Use elevation consistently
Practical UI L05: Use depth to support navigation and priority

elements.name: Layers (z-index)
elements.summary: A fixed stacking order from page content to the skip link.
elements.why: A named stacking order prevents the 'z-index: 9999' arms race and guarantees, for example, that a save toast is never hidden behind a dialog (Peak–end rule: the end of an action must be seen).
when: Anything positioned that must sit above or below something else.
how: Order: `layer-base` 0 < `raised` 1 < `sticky` 10 < `sidebar` 20 < `dropdown` 100 < `drawer` 150 < `dialog` 200 < `toast` 300 < `tooltip` 400 < `skip` 1000.
Use `z-index: var(--orca-layer-dropdown)`.
avoid: Raw z-index numbers.

examples.title: Using a layer
examples.html: Dropdown layer

law_names: Peak–end rule: people judge an experience by its peak and its end

elements.name: Control heights
elements.summary: Five heights shared by buttons, fields, selects and toggles: sm, dense, md, lg, xl.
elements.why: Controls that share a height line up in rows and toolbars (alignment), and the 44px touch minimum is applied in one place for every control (Fitts's law, Practical UI B11).
when: md (37px) by default; dense (29px) in top bars and filter bars; sm (22.5px) inside table rows; lg (44px) for touch-first screens; xl (48px) for phone primary actions.
how: Modifiers: `--sm`, `--dense`, `--lg`, `--xl` on `.orca-button`, `.orca-input`, `.orca-select`, `.orca-icon-button`.
On coarse pointers and below 620px every control grows to `--orca-control-lg` (44px) automatically.
avoid: Mixing heights in one row of controls.

examples.title: Heights side by side

law_names: Fitts's law: big, close, well-spaced targets are faster and safer
Practical UI B11: Make targets large and separated

elements.name: Motion
elements.summary: Four durations and two easings, all under the 400 ms Doherty threshold.
elements.why: Fast, consistent feedback keeps people in flow (Doherty threshold). Motion explains change; it never decorates. Reduced-motion users get the end state immediately (Von Restorff accessibility note).
when: snap 0.1s: hover on buttons, tabs, rows.
fast 0.165s: field fills, chevrons, card lift.
brisk 0.333s: ticks, switches, accordions, drawers, progress.
how: `transition: background-color var(--orca-duration-snap) var(--orca-ease-in)` for hover.
`var(--orca-ease-out)` for anything arriving.
ORCA's base layer stops animations for `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.
avoid: Animations longer than 0.333s on interface feedback.
Looping motion except spinners, skeletons and indeterminate progress.

examples.title: Hover speed
examples.html: <button class="orca-button" type="button">Hover me: 0.1s</button>

law_names: Doherty threshold: respond within 400 ms; show progress for anything slower
Von Restorff effect: the one thing that differs is noticed; use emphasis sparingly

elements.name: Aspect-ratio utilities
elements.summary: Reserve the space of images and video before they load.
elements.why: Reserving space stops the page jumping when media arrives, which feels faster and avoids mis-taps (Doherty threshold: perceived performance; Fitts's law).
when: Any image, video, snapshot or chart whose size is known only after loading.
how: Wrapper: `.orca-ratio.orca-ratio--16x9` (also 1x1, 4x3, 3x2, 21x9, 3x4) with the media inside.
Single element: `.orca-aspect-16x9` etc. Custom ratio: `style="--orca-ratio: 5 / 4"` on `.orca-ratio`.

examples.title: 16:9 frame

law_names: Doherty threshold: respond within 400 ms; show progress for anything slower

elements.name: Scrollbar style
elements.summary: A thin, token-coloured scrollbar for inner scrolling regions.
elements.why: Inner scroll areas need a visible cue that there is more content (Practical UI S06); a thin bar in `border-strong` stays visible without competing with content.
when: Scrolling panels, menus, code blocks, sidebars.
how: Add `.orca-scroll` to the element that scrolls; it sets `overflow: auto`.
avoid: Styling the page's main scrollbar; leave the OS default.

law_names: Practical UI S06: Make essential content visible or discoverable

elements.name: Heading (h1–h6)
elements.summary: Document headings from h1 to h6, plus a display style for marketing pages.
elements.why: A heading outline lets people scan and lets screen-reader users jump between sections (Miller's law: chunking; Practical UI W08). Tangerine's thin h2 is the system's typographic signature.
when: Structuring long content: docs, settings pages, reports.
Marketing pages: `.orca-display` for the one hero line.
how: Use real `<h1>`–`<h6>` elements with `.orca-h1`…`.orca-h6`.
One `<h1>` per page. Never skip a level going down.
h1 and h2 are 42/48 from 1036px and 32/40 below; h4 (light) suits dialog and empty-state titles.
Write in sentence case, no full stop (W02, W12).
avoid: Choosing a heading level for its size: keep levels in order and restyle with a class if needed.
Page and panel titles in applications: use `page-title` and `panel-title`.

elements.name: Button
elements.summary: A command. Variants express importance: primary, secondary (default), ghost, link, plus brand, danger, neutral, elevated and outlines.
elements.why: Three clearly different weights (filled, outlined, text) let people find the main action instantly and make the hierarchy survive colour-blindness (Practical UI B01, B02; Von Restorff effect). One primary action per screen keeps decisions fast (Hick's law, B03).
when: `orca-button--primary`: the one main action of the screen or form (Save, Add image).
default (no modifier): secondary actions and equal alternatives (Cancel, Export).
`--ghost`: low-priority or repeated actions in toolbars and rows.
`--danger`: only to confirm a destructive action inside a confirm dialog.
`--brand`: the single brand moment on a marketing or onboarding screen.
`--neutral`: filled grey for toggles and filter chips in toolbars.
`--elevated`: a button floating over media or maps.
`--outline-accent` / `--outline-danger`: a secondary action that needs a colour cue (a quiet first step of a delete).
how: `<button class="orca-button orca-button--primary" type="submit">Save image</button>`. Always set `type`.
Label: verb + object, one to three words, sentence case (B10).
Order: most important first, left to right; stack full width on phones (B08).
Icon + label: put `{% icon %}` before the text; the icon is decorative.
Busy: set `aria-busy="true"`, disable, and prepend ``.
Aliases kept from earlier systems: positive = primary, negative = danger, base = ghost, secondary = default.
avoid: Navigation: use a link.
Two primary buttons on one screen.
A red button as the first step of a delete (B13): use the default or `--outline-danger`, confirm with `--danger`.
'OK', 'Submit', 'Yes': name the action.
a11y: Focus ring is drawn inside the button; on filled variants it uses the on-fill colour so it shows.
Disabled buttons cannot be focused: explain why nearby or keep the button enabled and validate on press (B06, B07).

elements.summary: A single-line field: filled, square, with a 1.5px bottom border.
elements.why: Native inputs with a visible boundary and a persistent label are instantly recognisable (Jakob's law, Practical UI R07, R18). The right `type`, `inputmode` and `autocomplete` let phones and browsers do the typing (Tesler's law).
when: Short free text: names, addresses, numbers with units, codes.
how: `<input class="orca-input" id=… name=… type="text">` under an `orca-label`.

Space fields 24px apart and keep each label 8px above its own field, so a label never looks like the caption of the field before it (R10).

avoid: Choosing from fewer than ~10 known options: use radios or a select (R11).
Long text: use a textarea.
a11y: Field text is 16px on touch so iOS does not zoom.
Never put essential instructions in `placeholder`.

elements.why: Most form errors come from fields people misread. A fixed order (label, hint, error, control) means every field is read the same way, the hint is seen before answering and the error sits above the control where the keyboard cannot hide it (Practical UI R08, R10, R20). # videos/views.py — the dialog only confirms; the delete is a POST the server checks
from django.contrib import messages
from django.shortcuts import get_object_or_404, redirect
from django.views.decorators.http import require_POST

from .models import Video


@require_POST
def delete_video(request, pk):
    video = get_object_or_404(Video, pk=pk, owner=request.user)
    video.delete()
    messages.success(request, f"Video “{video}” deleted.")
    return redirect("video-list")

# videos/views.py (get_context_data of the page)
from django.db.models import Count
from django.db.models.functions import ExtractHour
from django.utils import timezone

today = timezone.localdate()

# videos/forms.py

# videos/views.py
from django.shortcuts import get_object_or_404, redirect, render

from .forms import ChapterFormSet
from .models import Video


def edit_chapters(request, pk):
    video = get_object_or_404(Video, pk=pk)
    formset = ChapterFormSet(request.POST or None, instance=video, prefix="chapters")
    if request.method == "POST" and formset.is_valid():
        formset.save()
        return redirect("video-detail", pk=video.pk)
    # Template: {{ formset.management_form }}, one [data-orca-row] per form, and a <template id="chapter-row">
    # holding {{ formset.empty_form }} (its names contain __prefix__). The add-row button points at it with
    # data-orca-add-row="chapter-row" and data-orca-total="id_chapters-TOTAL_FORMS".
    return render(request, "videos/chapters.html", {"video": video, "formset": formset})

from django import forms

    Video, Reminder, fields=["minutes_before", "method"], extra=0, can_delete=True,

# videos/views.py
from django.shortcuts import get_object_or_404, redirect, render

from .forms import ReminderFormSet
from .models import Video


def edit_reminders(request, pk):
    video = get_object_or_404(Video, pk=pk)
    formset = ReminderFormSet(request.POST or None, instance=video, prefix="reminders")
    if request.method == "POST" and formset.is_valid():
        formset.save()
        return redirect("video-detail", pk=video.pk)
    # Template: {{ formset.management_form }}, one [data-orca-row] per form, and a <template id="reminder-row">
    # holding {{ formset.empty_form }} (its names contain __prefix__). The add-row button points at it with
    # data-orca-add-row="reminder-row" and data-orca-total="id_reminders-TOTAL_FORMS".
    return render(request, "videos/reminders.html", {"video": video, "formset": formset})

# videos/forms.py
from django import forms

from .models import Chapter, Video

ChapterFormSet = forms.inlineformset_factory(
    Video, Chapter, fields=["title", "starts_at"], extra=0, can_delete=True,
)


# videos/views.py
from django.shortcuts import get_object_or_404, redirect, render

from .forms import ChapterFormSet
from .models import Video


def edit_chapters(request, pk):
    video = get_object_or_404(Video, pk=pk)
    formset = ChapterFormSet(request.POST or None, instance=video, prefix="chapters")
    if request.method == "POST" and formset.is_valid():
        formset.save()
        return redirect("video-detail", pk=video.pk)
    # Template: {{ formset.management_form }}, one [data-orca-row] per form, and a <template id="chapter-row">
    # holding {{ formset.empty_form }} (its names contain __prefix__). The add-row button points at it with
    # data-orca-add-row="chapter-row" and data-orca-total="id_chapters-TOTAL_FORMS".
    return render(request, "videos/chapters.html", {"video": video, "formset": formset})

# videos/forms.py
from django import forms

from .models import Album, Video


class VideoFilterForm(forms.Form):
    q = forms.CharField(label="Title contains", required=False)
    album = forms.ModelChoiceField(Album.objects.all(), required=False, empty_label="Any album")
    status = forms.MultipleChoiceField(choices=Video.Status.choices, required=False,
                                       widget=forms.CheckboxSelectMultiple)


# videos/views.py
from django.views.generic import ListView

from orca.mixins import OrcaPageMixin

from .forms import VideoFilterForm
from .models import Video


class VideoList(OrcaPageMixin, ListView):
    model = Video
    paginate_by = 25
    template_name = "orca/generic/list.html"   # or "orca/layouts/simple_data.html"
    list_columns = ["title", "album", "status", ("Views today", "views_today")]
    detail_url_name, create_url_name = "video-detail", "video-create"

    def get_queryset(self):
        qs = super().get_queryset()
        self.filter_form = VideoFilterForm(self.request.GET or None)
        if self.filter_form.is_valid():
            data = self.filter_form.cleaned_data
            if data["q"]:
                qs = qs.filter(title__icontains=data["q"])
            if data["album"]:
                qs = qs.filter(album=data["album"])
            if data["status"]:
                qs = qs.filter(status__in=data["status"])
        return qs

    def get_context_data(self, **kwargs):
        ctx = super().get_context_data(**kwargs)
        # The template puts the Filters button in the page actions and the form in the right drawer.
        ctx["filter_form"] = self.filter_form
        data = self.filter_form.cleaned_data if self.filter_form.is_valid() else {}
        ctx["active_filters"] = sum(1 for value in data.values() if value)
        return ctx

# videos/views.py
from django.contrib import messages
from django.shortcuts import redirect
from django.views.decorators.http import require_POST
from django.views.generic import ListView

from .models import Video

SORTABLE = {"title", "-title", "recorded_on", "-recorded_on", "views_today", "-views_today"}


class VideoList(ListView):
    model = Video
    paginate_by = 25

    def get_ordering(self):
        sort = self.request.GET.get("sort", "title")     # sortable headers link to ?sort=-recorded_on
        return sort if sort in SORTABLE else "title"

    def get_context_data(self, **kwargs):
        ctx = super().get_context_data(**kwargs)
        ctx["sort"] = self.get_ordering()                 # the header marks aria-sort from it
        return ctx


@require_POST
def bulk_archive(request):
    """The table is a form; each row checkbox is name="selected" value="{{ video.pk }}"."""
    ids = request.POST.getlist("selected")
    count = Video.objects.filter(pk__in=ids, owner=request.user).update(archived=True)
    messages.success(request, f"{count} videos archived.")
    return redirect("video-list")

# videos/views.py
import datetime as dt

from django.db.models import Count
from django.db.models.functions import ExtractHour, TruncDate
from django.utils import timezone
from django.views.generic import TemplateView

from .models import Visit


class ReportView(TemplateView):
    template_name = "videos/report.html"

    def get_context_data(self, **kwargs):
        ctx = super().get_context_data(**kwargs)
        today = timezone.localdate()
        start = today - dt.timedelta(days=6)
        # Categories as labels, one series per bar colour; stacked=True or horizontal=True.
        rows = (Visit.objects.filter(at__date__gte=start).annotate(day=TruncDate("at"))
                .values_list("day", "entrance").annotate(n=Count("id")))
        counts = {(day, entrance): n for day, entrance, n in rows}
        days = [start + dt.timedelta(days=i) for i in range(7)]
        entrances = sorted({entrance for _, entrance, _ in rows})
        ctx["visits"] = {"labels": [d.strftime("%a") for d in days],
                         "series": [{"name": e, "values": [counts.get((d, e), 0) for d in days]} for e in entrances]}
        # Template: {% orca_chart "bar" visits title="Visitors per day" subtitle="This week" %}
        return ctx

# videos/notifications.py
from django.core.mail import EmailMultiAlternatives
from django.template.loader import render_to_string
from django.utils.html import strip_tags


def send_offline_alert(video, recipients):
    context = {
        "title": f"{video} is offline",
        "preheader": f"No video since {video.last_seen:%H:%M}",
        "paragraphs": [f"{video} has sent nothing since {video.last_seen:%H:%M} today.",
                       "Check the network connection; playback restarts on its own."],
        "action_url": f"https://example.com{video.get_absolute_url()}",
        "action_label": "Open the video",
        "footer": "You get this email because you are on the alert list.",
    }
    html = render_to_string("orca/email/base.html", context)   # colours are inlined: no CSS needed
    message = EmailMultiAlternatives(context["title"], strip_tags(html), to=recipients)
    message.attach_alternative(html, "text/html")
    message.send()

class CalendarView(TemplateView):

    def get_context_data(self, **kwargs):
        ctx = super().get_context_data(**kwargs)
        today = timezone.localdate()
        month = dt.date.fromisoformat(self.request.GET.get("month", today.strftime("%Y-%m")) + "-01")
        # Events are dicts or objects with title, start, end (date or datetime), all_day, color (1–8 or a

             "color": e.calendar.color, "url": e.get_absolute_url(), "location": e.place}
            for e in Event.objects.filter(starts_at__date__lte=month + dt.timedelta(days=42),
                                          ends_at__date__gte=month - dt.timedelta(days=7))
        ]
        ctx["holidays"] = {"2026-11-11": "Armistice Day"}  # date → name
        ctx.update(month=month, today=today, now=timezone.localtime())
        return ctx

from django.shortcuts import get_object_or_404, redirect, render

from .forms import AvailabilityFormSet
from .models import Video


def edit_availabilitys(request, pk):
    video = get_object_or_404(Video, pk=pk)
    formset = AvailabilityFormSet(request.POST or None, instance=video, prefix="availabilitys")
    if request.method == "POST" and formset.is_valid():
        formset.save()
        return redirect("video-detail", pk=video.pk)
    # Template: {{ formset.management_form }}, one [data-orca-row] per form, and a <template id="availability-row">

    # data-orca-add-row="availability-row" and data-orca-total="id_availabilitys-TOTAL_FORMS".
    return render(request, "videos/availabilitys.html", {"video": video, "formset": formset})

elements.name: Kanban board
elements.summary: Columns of cards by status; cards move between columns by drag and drop or a 'Move to' menu, with work-in-progress limits.
elements.why: Columns make the flow of work visible and bottlenecks obvious (Practical UI L01, grouping); WIP limits that turn red when exceeded stop overloading (Von Restorff). The menu alternative makes moving possible by keyboard and touch.
when: Team workflows with a few stages: installation jobs, support tickets.
how: `<div class="orca-board" data-orca-board>` of `section.orca-board__col` each with a head (name, `[data-orca-count]` badge, `.orca-board__limit`) and `<ul class="orca-board__cards" data-orca-column="key">` of board cards with `draggable="true"` and an `id`.

elements.name: Page landmarks
elements.summary: The regions every page has: skip navigation, the main landmark and the place dialogs open in.
elements.why: Landmarks let assistive technology jump straight to the content (WCAG 1.3.1, 2.4.1) and give dialogs one place outside the content flow, so focus and stacking work the same on every page (Jakob's law, Tesler's law).
when: Every page: the base layout writes them, so pages never do.
how: `<body>` starts with the skip navigation; `<main id="main" tabindex="-1">` holds the content; dialogs and drawers go in `{% block modal %}` after `</main>`.
a11y: One `<main>` per page; dialogs outside it are opened with `showModal()` so the page behind is inert.

elements.name: Base layout
elements.summary: The root every ORCA page extends: the html element with language, theme and density, the head with ORCA's styles and theme bootstrap, the skip link, and slots for body, modal and scripts.
elements.why: Every page needs the same document skeleton, and getting it slightly wrong breaks accessibility (no language, no skip link) or causes a flash of the wrong theme. One base removes that whole class of mistakes (Tesler's law).

server.title: Sending the email
server.python:
# videos/notifications.py
from django.core.mail import EmailMultiAlternatives
from django.template.loader import render_to_string
from django.utils.html import strip_tags


def send_offline_alert(video, recipients):
    context = {
        "title": f"{video} is offline",
        "preheader": f"No video since {video.last_seen:%H:%M}",
        "paragraphs": [f"{video} has sent nothing since {video.last_seen:%H:%M} today.",
                       "Check the network connection; playback restarts on its own."],
        "action_url": f"https://example.com{video.get_absolute_url()}",
        "action_label": "Open the video",
        "footer": "You get this email because you are on the alert list.",
    }
    html = render_to_string("orca/email/base.html", context)   # colours are inlined: no CSS needed
    message = EmailMultiAlternatives(context["title"], strip_tags(html), to=recipients)
    message.attach_alternative(html, "text/html")
    message.send()

context: `title`, `preheader`, `paragraphs`, `action_url`, `action_label`, `footer`, `lang`.

# videos/views.py
from django.views.generic import TemplateView


class Home(TemplateView):
    template_name = "orca/layouts/home.html"

    def get_context_data(self, **kwargs):
        ctx = super().get_context_data(**kwargs)
        user = self.request.user
        ctx["title"] = f"Good morning, {user.first_name}"
        ctx["stats"] = [
            {"label": "Views today", "value": f"{views_today():,}", "icon": "show", "url": "/reports/"},
            {"label": "Videos", "value": Video.objects.count(), "icon": "play", "foot": "3 processing"},
        ]
        ctx["shortcuts"] = [{"label": "Add a video", "url": "/videos/new/", "icon": "plus"},
                            {"label": "Open reports", "url": "/reports/", "icon": "statistics"}]
        return ctx

from django.views.generic import ListView

from orca.mixins import OrcaPageMixin

from .forms import VideoFilterForm
from .models import Video


class VideoList(OrcaPageMixin, ListView):
    model = Video
    paginate_by = 25
    template_name = "orca/generic/list.html"   # or "orca/layouts/simple_data.html"
    list_columns = ["title", "album", "status", ("Views today", "views_today")]
    detail_url_name, create_url_name = "video-detail", "video-create"

    def get_queryset(self):
        qs = super().get_queryset()
        self.filter_form = VideoFilterForm(self.request.GET or None)
        if self.filter_form.is_valid():
            data = self.filter_form.cleaned_data
            if data["q"]:
                qs = qs.filter(title__icontains=data["q"])
            if data["album"]:
                qs = qs.filter(album=data["album"])
            if data["status"]:
                qs = qs.filter(status__in=data["status"])
        return qs

    def get_context_data(self, **kwargs):
        ctx = super().get_context_data(**kwargs)
        # The template puts the Filters button in the page actions and the form in the right drawer.
        ctx["filter_form"] = self.filter_form
        data = self.filter_form.cleaned_data if self.filter_form.is_valid() else {}
        ctx["active_filters"] = sum(1 for value in data.values() if value)
        return ctx

# videos/views.py
from django.shortcuts import get_object_or_404
from django.urls import reverse
from django.views.generic import DetailView, ListView

from orca.mixins import OrcaPageMixin

from .models import Album, Video


class AlbumTabs(OrcaPageMixin):
    """The parent (an album) and its tabs, for every page under /albums/<album_pk>/."""

    def get_parent(self):
        return get_object_or_404(Album, pk=self.kwargs["album_pk"])

    def get_context_data(self, **kwargs):
        ctx = super().get_context_data(**kwargs)
        album = ctx["parent"] = self.get_parent()
        here = self.request.path
        tabs = [("Overview", reverse("album-detail", args=[album.pk]), None),
                ("Videos", reverse("album-videos", args=[album.pk]), album.videos.count())]
        ctx["parent_tabs"] = [{"label": label, "url": url, "count": count, "current": here == url} for label, url, count in tabs]
        ctx["parent_stats"] = [{"label": "Videos", "value": album.videos.count(), "icon": "play"},
                               {"label": "Last change", "value": album.updated_at.strftime("%-d %b"), "icon": "history"}]
        ctx["parent_update_url"] = reverse("album-update", args=[album.pk])
        return ctx


class AlbumDetail(AlbumTabs, DetailView):
    model = Album
    pk_url_kwarg = "album_pk"
    template_name = "orca/generic/parent_detail.html"
    detail_fields = ["title", "owner", "created_at"]

    detail_url_name, create_url_name = "video-detail", "album-video-create"

import datetime as dt

from django.urls import reverse
from django.utils import timezone
from django.views.generic import TemplateView

from .models import Calendar, Event


class CalendarPage(TemplateView):
    template_name = "orca/layouts/calendar.html"

    def get_context_data(self, **kwargs):
        ctx = super().get_context_data(**kwargs)
        today = timezone.localdate()
        view = self.request.GET.get("view", "month")                  # month, week, day or agenda
        day = dt.date.fromisoformat(self.request.GET.get("day", today.isoformat()))
        month = day.replace(day=1)
        step = {"month": dt.timedelta(days=31), "week": dt.timedelta(days=7)}.get(view, dt.timedelta(days=1))
        url = lambda d, v=view: f"?view={v}&day={d.isoformat()}"
        ctx.update(
            title="Calendar", view=view, day=day, month=month, today=today, now=timezone.localtime(),
            # Events: dicts (or objects) with title, start, end, all_day, color, url, location, status.
            events=[{"title": e.title, "start": e.starts_at, "end": e.ends_at, "all_day": e.all_day,
                     "color": e.calendar.color, "url": e.get_absolute_url(), "location": e.place}
                    for e in Event.objects.filter(starts_at__date__gte=month - dt.timedelta(days=7),
                                                  starts_at__date__lte=month + dt.timedelta(days=42))],
            holidays={"2026-11-11": "Armistice Day"},
            period_title=day.strftime("%B %Y") if view == "month" else day.strftime("%-d %B %Y"),
            prev_url=url(day - step), next_url=url(day + step), today_url=url(today),
            day_url="?view=day&day={date}", month_url="?view=month&day={month}-01",
            views=[{"label": v.title(), "url": url(day, v), "current": v == view} for v in ("month", "week", "day", "agenda")],
            calendars=[{"key": c.slug, "label": c.name, "color": c.color, "checked": True} for c in Calendar.objects.all()],
            create_url=reverse("event-create"),
        )
        return ctx

    def get_context_data(self, **kwargs):
        ctx = super().get_context_data(**kwargs)
        today = timezone.localdate()
        start = dt.date.fromisoformat(self.request.GET.get("start", (today - dt.timedelta(days=today.weekday())).isoformat()))
        # Rows: label, start, end (dates, end included), progress 0–100, state "done" or "late", url, milestone.
        ctx["rows"] = [{"label": t.title, "start": t.starts_on, "end": t.due_on, "progress": t.progress,
                        "state": "done" if t.done else ("late" if t.due_on < today else ""), "url": t.get_absolute_url()}
                       for t in Task.objects.filter(due_on__gte=start)]
        ctx.update(title="Timeline", start=start, days=14, today=today,
                   period_title=f"{start:%-d %b} – {start + dt.timedelta(days=13):%-d %b %Y}",
                   prev_url=f"?start={start - dt.timedelta(days=14)}", next_url=f"?start={start + dt.timedelta(days=14)}",
                   today_url="?")
        return ctx

from django.shortcuts import redirect, render

STEPS = ["Service", "Date and time", "Your details", "Confirm"]


def book_time(request):
    chosen = request.session.setdefault("booking", {})

from django.views.generic import ListView

from orca.mixins import OrcaPageMixin

from .forms import VideoFilterForm
from .models import Video


class VideoList(OrcaPageMixin, ListView):
    model = Video
    paginate_by = 25
    template_name = "orca/layouts/simple_data.html"
    list_columns = ["title", "album", "status", ("Views today", "views_today")]
    detail_url_name, create_url_name = "video-detail", "video-create"

    def get_queryset(self):
        qs = super().get_queryset()
        self.filter_form = VideoFilterForm(self.request.GET or None)
        if self.filter_form.is_valid():
            data = self.filter_form.cleaned_data
            if data["q"]:
                qs = qs.filter(title__icontains=data["q"])
            if data["album"]:
                qs = qs.filter(album=data["album"])
            if data["status"]:
                qs = qs.filter(status__in=data["status"])
        return qs

    def get_context_data(self, **kwargs):
        ctx = super().get_context_data(**kwargs)
        # The template puts the Filters button in the page actions and the form in the right drawer.
        ctx["filter_form"] = self.filter_form
        data = self.filter_form.cleaned_data if self.filter_form.is_valid() else {}
        ctx["active_filters"] = sum(1 for value in data.values() if value)
        return ctx

elements.why: Layouts own this slot; a page that replaces it loses the shell (Tesler's law), so only new layouts override it.
when: Pages built on every layout (from orca/layouts/base.html).
how: `{% block body %}…{% endblock %}` in a template that extends every layout (from orca/layouts/base.html).
Override it only in your own layout that extends `orca/layouts/base.html`.

examples.title: {% block body %}
examples.html: {% templatetag openblock %} block body {% templatetag closeblock %}<main id="main" tabindex="-1">…</main>{% templatetag openblock %} endblock {% templatetag closeblock %}

law_names: Tesler's law: move unavoidable complexity from the user to the system

elements.name: Modal
elements.summary: Dialogs and drawers, placed after the page so they open above everything.
elements.why: Dialogs outside the main content avoid clipping and stacking problems and are found by assistive technology in one place (Practical UI L05).
when: Pages built on every layout (from orca/layouts/base.html).
how: `{% block modal %}…{% endblock %}` in a template that extends every layout (from orca/layouts/base.html).
Put `<dialog>` elements here and open them with `data-orca-dialog-open`.

examples.title: {% block modal %}
examples.html:
{% block modal %}

Dialog title

Dialog text.

{% endblock %}

law_names: Practical UI L05: Use depth to support navigation and priority

elements.name: Footer
elements.summary: The end of the page: legal and help links on public pages, a version line in applications.
elements.why: People look for legal and help links at the bottom (Jakob's law).
when: Pages built on the app shell and every template built on it (generic, parent-child and page-type templates), auth, marketing and docs layouts.
how: `{% block footer %}…{% endblock %}` in a template that extends the app shell and every template built on it (generic, parent-child and page-type templates), auth, marketing and docs layouts.
The marketing layout fills it from `footer_cols`; in the app shell it sits at the end of the main column.

examples.title: {% block footer %}
examples.html:
{% block footer %}

Version 0.4.0 · Help

{% endblock %}

law_names: Jakob's law: work the way products people already know work

elements.name: Extra head
elements.summary: Page-specific additions to the head: a stylesheet, meta tags, preloads.
elements.why: Keeping page additions in their own slot means the shared head is never copied (and never drifts) (Practical UI F09).
when: Pages built on every layout (from orca/layouts/base.html).
how: `{% block extra_head %}…{% endblock %}` in a template that extends every layout (from orca/layouts/base.html).
Use it for one page's CSS or meta; never redefine ORCA tokens other than the brand ones.

examples.title: {% block extra_head %}
examples.html: {% templatetag openblock %} block extra_head {% templatetag closeblock %}<meta name="robots" content="noindex">{% templatetag openblock %} endblock {% templatetag closeblock %}

law_names: Practical UI F09: Keep visual and functional behaviour consistent

elements.name: Extra scripts
elements.summary: One page's scripts, after the site-wide ones.
elements.why: A page's script loads only where it is needed, keeping other pages fast (Doherty threshold).
when: Pages built on every layout (from orca/layouts/base.html).
how: `{% block extra_scripts %}…{% endblock %}` in a template that extends every layout (from orca/layouts/base.html).
Add `defer`; prefer ORCA's data attributes before writing script.

examples.title: {% block extra_scripts %}
examples.html: {% templatetag openblock %} block extra_scripts {% templatetag closeblock %}<script src="/static/app/reports.js" defer></script>{% templatetag openblock %} endblock {% templatetag closeblock %}

law_names: Doherty threshold: respond within 400 ms; show progress for anything slower

elements.name: Theme bootstrap
elements.summary: The inline script that applies the reader's saved theme before the page paints.
elements.why: Without it, a reader who chose dark sees a white flash on every page (Aesthetic–usability effect).
when: Pages built on every layout (from orca/layouts/base.html).
how: `{% block theme_bootstrap %}…{% endblock %}` in a template that extends every layout (from orca/layouts/base.html).
Defaults to `orca_theme_bootstrap`, which outputs nothing when the theme is fixed in settings; empty it if your CSP forbids inline scripts and you fix the theme.

examples.title: {% block theme_bootstrap %}
examples.html: {% templatetag openblock %} block theme_bootstrap {% templatetag closeblock %}{% templatetag openblock %} orca_theme_bootstrap {% templatetag closeblock %}{% templatetag openblock %} endblock {% templatetag closeblock %}

law_names: Aesthetic–usability effect: consistent, careful visuals earn trust

elements.name: List actions
elements.summary: The buttons of a list page: Add first, then exports or bulk tools.
elements.why: The create button in the same place on every list is found without looking (Jakob's law); one primary keeps it obvious (Practical UI B03).
when: Pages built on the generic list, parent-child list and simple data page templates.
how: `{% block list_actions %}…{% endblock %}` in a template that extends the generic list, parent-child list and simple data page templates.
Defaults to 'Add <model>' when `create_url` is set.

examples.title: {% block list_actions %}
examples.html: {% block list_actions %}{% icon "plus" %}Add video{% endblock %}

law_names: Jakob's law: work the way products people already know work
Practical UI B03: One primary action

elements.name: Detail actions
elements.summary: The buttons of a record: Edit, then other actions, Delete last and quieter.
elements.why: Edit and Delete in the same place on every record (Jakob's law), Delete apart and outlined so it is not hit by mistake (Practical UI B13).
when: Pages built on the generic detail, parent and parent-child detail templates.
how: `{% block detail_actions %}…{% endblock %}` in a template that extends the generic detail, parent and parent-child detail templates.
Defaults to Edit and Delete when `update_url` and `delete_url` are set.
